summary.headline: A good bank just above the buy price: Rs 148 against a Rs 144 buy price, after the dividend model was moved onto the shared code
summary.text: Sampath Bank (SAMP.N0000) is a well-run, well-capitalised bank, and at Rs 148.25 it sits about 3% above my new buy price of Rs 144. Nothing in the business has changed since the 14 November rebuild: nine-month group profit rose 15% to Rs 26.5bn (EPS Rs 22.63), but profit before tax was flat (−1%) because the growth came from a one-off lower tax charge; loans grew 22% and Stage 3 loans fell to 6.07%. It trades at 0.86x group NAV of Rs 173.18, 4.8x trailing earnings (5.4x with a normal tax rate) and a 6.9% dividend yield. Fair value falls to about Rs 169 (Rs 186 before) because all four methods are now worked by the site's shared formulas: the dividend model now keeps today's 37% payout instead of raising it to about 63% after five years, which the formula can't do, so it gives Rs 133 instead of Rs 194. Buy up to Rs 144; Rs 127 or less is a strong buy. Main risks: capital (CET1 12.27%), impairments as the new loans season, and a provisional beta to check in January.

quality.reason: A strong bank: ROE near 18% for three years, capital above minimums, profit every year and a steady cash dividend.

tests.label: Net debt no more than equity
tests.note: A bank, so judged on capital: CET1 12.27% (minimum 8.0%), total capital 15.32% (minimum 13.5%). Headroom is shrinking as loans grow; the Rs 10bn Tier 2 issue in October adds roughly 0.8 points (my estimate).

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: Profit in every year of the ten-year record, including the 2022 crisis. Caveat: 2024 had an Rs 11.7bn impairment reversal and 2026 a lower tax charge, so headline growth overstates the trend.

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends
tests.note: All-cash dividends of about 40% of bank profit since 2023 (Rs 10.30 for 2025).

The higher, 0.70, is used. Refresh in January 2027.

highlights.title: Nine months to September 2026 (group, unaudited)
highlights.text: Profit after tax up 15% to Rs 26.5bn; EPS Rs 22.63 against Rs 19.74. Profit before tax was flat at Rs 37.8bn (−1%); the gain came from income tax falling to Rs 11.3bn from Rs 14.9bn (29.8% of pre-tax profit against 39.1%) as prior-year assessments were settled.

highlights.title: The third quarter
highlights.text: Group pre-tax profit Rs 11.2bn, down 7%; after-tax profit Rs 8.7bn, up 15% on a tax charge of Rs 2.5bn (Rs 4.6bn a year earlier). A Rs 4.8bn trading loss in the quarter was partly offset by Rs 3.6bn of other operating income (exchange income rose as the rupee fell).

highlights.title: What drove income
highlights.text: Bank net interest income up 15% (margin 4.22% from 4.11%), fees up 21%, exchange income up 67% to Rs 5.9bn as the rupee fell Rs 20.63 against the dollar. Gains from selling bonds fell to Rs 1.1bn from Rs 3.8bn.

highlights.title: Costs and provisions
highlights.text: Operating costs up 22%, against income up 14%: cost-to-income 44.3% (41.5% a year earlier). Loan impairment Rs 8.1bn against Rs 2.3bn, from Rs 273bn of loan growth and extra buffers, offset by a Rs 1.3bn reversal on dollar bonds after Fitch upgraded Sri Lanka.

highlights.title: Loans, asset quality and capital
highlights.text: Gross loans up 22% to Rs 1.50tn; deposits up 12% to Rs 1.83tn. Gross Stage 3 6.07% (8.37% in December), coverage 68.7%. CET1 12.27%, total capital 15.32%. Rs 10bn of green bonds in July and Rs 10bn of Basel III debentures (12.8–13.0%) in October.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: (Long-run ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth) × NAV Rs 173.18: 0.76x / 1.06x / 1.59x book, with ROE 14% / 16% / 18%, growth 5% / 6% / 7%.

models.name: P/E method
models.comment: 2027 EPS Rs 27 / 30.5 / 33.5 × 4.5 / 5.5 / 6.5. EPS assumes a normal ~38% tax rate again, so the bear case is 12% below the Rs 30.66 run-rate, which is flattered by the 2026 tax settlement. The P/Es are within the bank's 2022–2025 range and below the justified 5.7x / 7.1x / 9.5x.

models.name: Dividend model
models.comment: Next year's dividend Rs 10.0 / 11.3 / 12.4 (37% of 2027 EPS, as now: 40% of bank profit), growing with profit at 6% / 9% / 11% for five years (capped at the 11.3% supported), then 5% / 6% / 7%, at the cost of equity. The payout stays at 37%, so profit kept beyond what growth needs isn't counted: a conservative, dividends-as-paid view. If the payout rose to 1 − growth ÷ ROE (about 63%) after five years, as the 14 November version assumed, this method would give about Rs 194 and fair value about Rs 185.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Used instead of a cash-flow DCF, which doesn't suit a bank. Book Rs 173.18 plus profit above the cost of equity: ROE moves in a straight line from 16.5% (2026 with a normal tax rate) to 14% / 16% / 18% over ten years, 37% payout, then the excess return grows at 5% / 6% / 7%.

modelsNote: A bank's cash flows are mostly lending and deposits, so instead of a cash-flow DCF I used residual income and a justified price-to-book, alongside P/E and dividends, all at the 15.4% cost of equity (16.9% / 13.9% bear / bull) and all worked by scripts/valuation.py. Growth check: assumed 6% / 9% / 11% a year for the next five years against 11.3% supported (63% of profit kept × 17.9% ROE); all within 2 points. Long-run growth 5–7% stays below the 12.24% bond yield, and needs 33–39% of profit kept. The dividend model is the lowest because it keeps today's 37% payout.

assumptions.label: Profit and dividend growth, next five years

scenarios.common: Cost of equity from the house formula (risk-free 8.24% + beta 0.70 × 10.28% equity premium). 2027 EPS assumes the tax rate returns to about 38% (2025: 38.6%) and pre-tax profit grows about 10% from a flat 2026 (bear: flat; bull: +18%). Shares 1,172.7m, none issued in 2024–2025.

sensitivity.title: Residual income base case, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Today's Rs 148.25 is close to a 16.9% cost of equity with a 14% long-run ROE (residual income), and on price to book it implies a long-run ROE of about 14%, below the 16–18% of the last three years.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 68,250 in total, against Rs 74,125 for 500 shares at Rs 148.25.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 144 needs a 3% fall from Rs 148.25 and has traded this year; Rs 136 (an 8% fall) is just above the 2026 low of Rs 135.50 (July–September). Rs 127 (a 14% fall) is below anything traded in 2026, so the last tier may not fill.

higher: Pre-tax profit growing again (2026 is flat so far).
Impairments settling back as the 2026 loans season well.
Lower interest rates, which would lower the cost of equity.
Cost growth slowing below income growth.
A cash dividend of Rs 12+ for 2026.
lower: A beta check in January that raises the cost of equity (each 1.5 points is worth about Rs 30–35 a share).
Capital used up by fast loan growth: smaller cash dividends, a scrip dividend or a rights issue (CET1 is 12.27%).
A provisioning cycle as the 2026 loan growth seasons.
The tax rate not returning to normal, or new taxes on banks.
Costs rising faster than income (up 22% against 14%).
Stress in the government-bond market (the bank holds about Rs 650bn of debt securities).

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2025 annual report and the 2026 interim reports to September 2026. The interim figures are unaudited, the beta is provisional, and the price is the CSE close of 20 November 2026, so check it before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

Decision box.Verdict: Watch list: Rs 148.25 is 12% below fair value of Rs 169 but about 3% above the Rs 144 buy price.
Decision box.Expected yearly return at Rs 148.25: About 17% a year if the price stays near 0.86x book: dividend 6.9% plus book growth of about 10%. More if the price moves towards fair value.
Decision box.Downside / upside: Bear case Rs 118 (−20%); bull case Rs 249 (+68%).
Decision box.What the price assumes: At 0.86x NAV, with 6% long-run growth and a 15.4% cost of equity, a long-run ROE of about 14%: below the 16–18% of the last three years.
Decision box.Confidence: Medium: price to book, P/E and residual income agree (Rs 168–191 base); the dividend model is lower (Rs 132) because it keeps today's payout. The beta is provisional and 2026 profit growth is mostly a tax saving.
Decision box.Margin of safety: Not yet: wait for Rs 144 or lower.

Business and moat.What it does: A Sri Lankan commercial bank with 230 branches, Rs 1.5tn of loans and Rs 1.83tn of deposits (bank, September 2026). Subsidiaries include Siyapatha Finance (leasing), Sampath Centre (property), Sampath Securities and Sampath Information Solutions; a wealth-management company is being set up.
Business and moat.Moat: Narrow: a strong retail and SME franchise, good digital channels and a 34% CASA ratio, but banking in Sri Lanka is competitive and regulated.
Business and moat.Growth: Loans grew 31% (net) in 2025 and 22% (gross) in nine months of 2026, faster than deposits; capital is the limit.

Accounting quality.Underlying earnings: The 2026 tax charge is low (29.8% of pre-tax profit against 39.1%) because prior-year assessments were finalised; the amount isn't disclosed. Taxed at the 2025 rate, trailing group EPS would be about Rs 27.6 against Rs 30.66 reported (my estimate).
Accounting quality.One-offs: 2024 profit included an Rs 11.7bn impairment reversal; 2026 includes Rs 1.3bn of reversals on dollar bonds.
Accounting quality.Presentation: Recoveries of written-off loans are now netted within impairment (comparatives reclassified; profit unaffected).
Accounting quality.Other comprehensive income: The FVOCI reserve fell Rs 5.2bn in nine months as bond prices fell; it goes straight to equity, not profit.

Sri Lanka checks.Interest rates: Watch: 10-year bond about 12.2%; rising rates cut bond values (FVOCI) and lift deposit costs, but lending rates (AWPLR) have risen with them, lifting the margin to 4.22%.
Sri Lanka checks.Rupee: Watch: down Rs 20.63 against the dollar in nine months; this lifted exchange income to Rs 5.9bn.
Sri Lanka checks.Tax and regulation: Risk: banks pay VAT and the social security levy on financial services as well as income tax; any budget change hits profit directly.
Sri Lanka checks.Dependence on the state: Watch: large holdings of government securities (about Rs 650bn of debt instruments at amortised cost and FVOCI).

Crisis stress test (2022-style).What happened in 2022: Bank impairment Rs 62.7bn (5.97% cost of risk) against Rs 17.1bn in 2021; profit still rose 5% to Rs 13.1bn on exchange gains; CET1 fell to 11.92%; the share price fell to Rs 26.00 (0.31x book); the dividend was partly paid in shares.
Crisis stress test (2022-style).Today: With CET1 at 12.27% before such a shock, a repeat would probably mean a scrip dividend or a rights issue, and the share price could halve. The bank would very likely stay profitable.

Investment case and sell rules.Why own it: A well-run bank with ROE near 18%, falling bad loans, a 6.7% cash dividend, at below book value.
Investment case and sell rules.The case is broken if: ROE falls below 14% for a full year, Stage 3 rises back above 8%, or capital forces a rights issue at a low price.
Investment case and sell rules.Sell triggers: Price more than 30% above fair value (above Rs 220); the case breaks; or a clearly better opportunity appears.

What this analysis doesn't cover: Damodaran's sector-beta pages and the local beta pages couldn't be opened in this run (blocked by the network settings); the beta of 0.70 rests on web-search extracts and should be rechecked in January 2027.
The amount of the prior-year tax settlement isn't disclosed, so the normal-tax EPS of about Rs 27.6 is my estimate.
Peer banks (COMB, HNB) weren't compared in this run.
Sampath's own 2027 guidance (none in the reports read).
fullText:
Summary: Sampath Bank (SAMP.N0000) is a well-run, well-capitalised bank, and at Rs 148.25 it sits about 3% above my new buy price of Rs 144. Nothing in the business has changed since the 14 November rebuild: nine-month group profit rose 15% to Rs 26.5bn (EPS Rs 22.63), but profit before tax was flat (−1%) because the growth came from a one-off lower tax charge; loans grew 22% and Stage 3 loans fell to 6.07%. It trades at 0.86x group NAV of Rs 173.18, 4.8x trailing earnings (5.4x with a normal tax rate) and a 6.9% dividend yield. Fair value falls to about Rs 169 (Rs 186 before) because all four methods are now worked by the site's shared formulas: the dividend model now keeps today's 37% payout instead of raising it to about 63% after five years, which the formula can't do, so it gives Rs 133 instead of Rs 194. Buy up to Rs 144; Rs 127 or less is a strong buy. Main risks: capital (CET1 12.27%), impairments as the new loans season, and a provisional beta to check in January.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 148.25, the CSE close on 20 November 2026 (Rs 154.00 on 13 November). It closed September at Rs 140.00; the 2026 range to September is Rs 135.50–167.00.
Nine months to September 2026 (group, unaudited): profit before tax Rs 37.8bn (−1%); income tax Rs 11.3bn (−24%); profit after tax Rs 26.5bn (+15%); EPS Rs 22.63 against Rs 19.74. Third quarter: pre-tax −7%, after-tax +15%.
Drivers: net interest income +15% (margin 4.22%), fees +21%, exchange income +67%; bond-sale gains down; costs +22% (cost-to-income 44.3%); loan impairments Rs 8.1bn against Rs 2.3bn.
Balance sheet: gross loans Rs 1.50tn (+22%), deposits Rs 1.83tn, gross Stage 3 6.07% (coverage 68.7%), CET1 12.27%, total capital 15.32%. Rs 10bn green bonds (July) and Rs 10bn Basel III debentures (October).
2025 (group): profit Rs 32.6bn, EPS Rs 27.77, dividend Rs 10.30, NAV Rs 165.23; bank ROE 17.9%.

Required return
Cost of equity = 8.24% risk-free (12.24% bond less 4.0% default spread) + 0.70 beta × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 15.4%; bear 16.9%, bull 13.9%. The bond rate hasn't moved since 14 November. The beta is provisional (web-search extracts; Damodaran's site couldn't be opened): refresh in January.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Justified price to book | 131.0 | 184.2 | 276.1 | 186.6
P/E method | 121.5 | 167.8 | 217.8 | 163.9
Dividend model | 86.5 | 131.7 | 204.0 | 132.6
Residual income | 132.5 | 190.6 | 297.7 | 194.6
Average | 117.9 | 168.6 | 248.9 | 169

What changed in this redo (21 November)
No new report; the record's figures were re-checked and the brief re-applied. All four methods are now worked by scripts/valuation.py, so the site's What if? panel can redo them. Two changes follow from that. The dividend model keeps the 37% payout throughout (the formula can't raise it after five years), which cuts it from Rs 194 to Rs 133; with the payout rising to about 63%, fair value would be about Rs 185. Residual income now starts every case at the same 16.5% ROE (2026 with a normal tax rate) instead of 15% / 17% / 18.5%. Price Rs 154 → Rs 148.25. Fair value Rs 186 → Rs 169, buy Rs 158 → Rs 144, strong buy Rs 139 → Rs 127.

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity 16.9% / 15.4% / 13.9%; long-run ROE 14% / 16% / 18%; ROE path from 16.5% to 14% / 16% / 18%; growth for five years 6% / 9% / 11% (supported 11.3%); long-run growth 5% / 6% / 7%; 2027 EPS 27 × 4.5 / 30.5 × 5.5 / 33.5 × 6.5; next year's dividend Rs 10.0 / 11.3 / 12.4, 37% payout.

Business tests: 4 of 4 passed; a good business but above the buy price: watch list (category 2, from buy now).

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 144, 150 up to Rs 136, 150 up to Rs 127: about Rs 68,250 in total. Rs 127 is below the 2026 low so far.

Management plans and shareholders: not yet in this analysis (no report was read in this redo); a /redo SAMP full would add them from the annual report and the September interim.
